title: HIPAA BAAs for OPI, VRI, and AI Interpreter Vendors
summary: Learn when HIPAA requires a BAA for medical interpreter vendors and what healthcare teams should review for OPI, VRI, AI, PHI, and subprocessors.
body_markdown:
###


No. A workforce interpreter generally does not need a separate BAA. An outside interpreter vendor acting on behalf of a covered entity will often be a business associate and require a BAA.


###


An ongoing contractual relationship with an outside telephone interpreter service will commonly fall under HIPAA's business-associate requirements.


###


If an outside VRI vendor handles PHI while providing interpretation on behalf of the covered entity, the relationship will commonly require a BAA.


###


If the AI vendor creates, receives, maintains, or transmits ePHI on behalf of the covered entity, it will generally be acting as a business associate and a BAA is typically required.


###


No. The organization still needs to review the actual PHI flow, safeguards, retention, subprocessors, access controls, incident response, and how the service fits into its HIPAA risk analysis.
